sections.topic: Reservation · Backward Classes in the Constitution
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-5 › Reservation - constitutional basis, Indra Sawhney, creamy layer, EWS reservation, promotion in reservation › Backward Classes in the Constitution
bullets: "Backward Classes" is not defined in the Constitution (APPSC G2 2017 key: the "defined" statement is the wrong one).

27% OBC quota in central jobs from 1993; in central educational institutions under the CEI (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006, in force Jan 2007 (IYB 2026 says 2007) after the 2005 amendment to Art. 15 (IYB) [GK for the Act's year].
NCBC: constitutional body under Art. 338B, examines inclusion/exclusion requests (APPCA Apr 2026).

Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006 (in force 2007): 27% OBC seats in central institutions (IYB; GS 2007 key: 93rd Amendment); OBC = classes "so determined by the Central Government" (APP).

sections.topic: Indra Sawhney and creamy layer link to NCBC
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-3 › National Commission for SCs (338), STs (338A) and Backward Classes (338B); Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities (350B) › Indra Sawhney and creamy layer link to NCBC
bullets: *Indra Sawhney v UoI* (16 Nov 1992) upheld 27% OBC reservation, introduced the creamy layer, and directed a permanent body for OBC-list inclusion/exclusion → NCBC Act, 1993 (in force 2 April 1993).
102nd Amendment Act, 2018 inserted Art. 338B - NCBC became constitutional; composition: Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and 3 members appointed by the President; civil court powers.
The 102nd Amendment also removed backward classes from the NCSC's purview .
105th Amendment, 2021 restored the States' power to prepare their own SEBC lists (after the Maratha quota judgment) .

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-1 › Right to Equality - Articles 14-18; reasonable classification, reservation jurisprudence › Reservation cases - ruling issue, creamy layer and 50% ceiling origin
bullets: M.R. Balaji: Year 1963; Ruling Reservation should generally stay below 50%
Indra Sawhney: Year 1992; Ruling 27% OBC quota upheld; creamy layer excluded; 50% ceiling; no reservation in promotions [GK for last two]
Indra Sawhney (16 Nov 1992): Issue decided 9-judge bench, 6:3: 27% OBC quota valid with creamy layer out; 50% cap; no reservation in promotion (UPSC; IYB)

Maratha case (Jaishri Patil, 2021): Issue decided Maratha quota struck down for crossing 50% without exceptional circumstances; read the 102nd Amendment as making the Central list the only SEBC list (UPSC)
M.R. Balaji v State of Mysore (1962): Held Caste cannot be the sole test; reservation must be reasonable, below 50% (APP's case table dates it 1960)

sections.topic: Transgender persons · Reservation and state measures
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-5 › Transgender persons - NALSA judgment, Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act 2019 › Reservation and state measures - horizontal vs vertical, first service quota, AP pensions, welfare board, ID cards
bullets: Debate: NALSA (2014) asked governments to treat transgender persons as socially and educationally backward (a vertical OBC-type quota); the community seeks horizontal reservation cutting across SC/ST/OBC/General. The issue resurfaced in June 2023 with a Mumbai protest against Maharashtra's reply to the Bombay High Court (APPSC 2022).
Karnataka - first State to give 1% reservation to transgender persons in all government services (July 2021) (APPSC 2023).

sections.topic: Agricultural inputs · Farm subsidies vs public investment
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-3 › Agricultural inputs - seeds, fertilisers and the subsidy regime, pesticides, mechanisation, extension services › Farm subsidies vs public investment - classifying input subsidies, MSP, research, irrigation
bullets: Input subsidies: fertiliser, power, irrigation water, seed, credit (interest subvention) - current transfers; public investment: irrigation projects, research, rural infrastructure - capital formation .
MSP = price support, not an input subsidy .
Debate: subsidies helped small farmers adopt HYV but mostly benefit prosperous regions and the fertiliser industry (APP).

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-5 › Compensation for loss of revenue and the development of backward districts (Rayalaseema and North Coastal) › Rayalaseema development issues - drought, irrigation deficit, industrial backwardness
bullets: Drought and low density: population density is low because of recurring droughts and famines (APP). Rayalaseema has 8 districts (Kurnool, Nandyal, Anantapur, Sri Satya Sai, YSR, Annamayya, Tirupati, Chittoor).
Godavari-Penna link, Phase I: Status / aim 73 TMC of Godavari flood water to the Pennar via a 5-stage lift; about 21% done

Strengths: a Horticulture Hub, holding 43% of AP's horticulture area and 52% of its output, with 71% of micro-irrigation. Six AP districts are in India's top 10 for micro-irrigation: five from Rayalaseema plus Prakasam.
Industrial backwardness: investment is skewed towards the coast. Rayalaseema lacks anchor industries, which leads to distress migration and agrarian crisis (CDI Block10).
Historical root: the Sri Bagh Pact (16 Nov 1937) promised Rayalaseema priority in irrigation for 10 years (APP).

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-3 › Agrarian crisis - causes, farmer distress and suicides, loan waivers, small-holding viability › Universal angles
bullets: Current relevance: Tenant Farmers' Association says 300+ farmer suicides since 2024 but only 112 recognised (TH, 27 Jan 2026); CM orders audit of every farmer suicide (TH, 28 Feb 2026).
Current relevance: Kharif 2026 El Nino deficit - farmer bodies demand loan relief; actual cultivators missing from e-crop records lose insurance and credit (TH, 28 Aug 2026).

Current relevance: AP has a severe rainfall deficit in 2026. The opposition cites a 54.73% deficit hitting 653 of 685 mandals and sowing at only 69% of normal, and demands a drought emergency (TH, 7 Sep 2026; opposition claim).

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-3 › Economic reforms of 1991 - background, stabilisation and structural adjustment measures › Globalisation - meaning, scope, impact
bullets: Integration of the domestic economy with the world through trade, capital, technology and labour flows ; excludes greater state control or reduced foreign trade.
Impact: trade in goods and services expanded, more FDI, access to foreign technology; but imports grew faster than exports (so "exports rose more than imports" is false - PYQ 2025).
Trade: rapid growth of both exports and imports, but imports grew faster than exports - so "exports rose more than imports" is not true (APPSC 2025).
Services: IT/outsourcing boom cushioned the CAD; 1,800+ Global Capability Centres earned $38.25 bn of services exports in July 2026 (LENSD, 3 Sep 2026).
Agriculture and employment: agriculture neglected; growth concentrated in capital-intensive sectors created too few jobs (CDI Beyond GDP essay).

bullets: Manual for Drought Management 2016 : rainfall deviation and dry spells are the mandatory indicators. Impact indicators (crop sowing, satellite vegetation index, soil moisture, hydrology) confirm the call. Drought is declared moderate or severe.
Crop Weather Watch Group (Ministry of Agriculture) meets weekly during the monsoon to track rainfall, sowing and reservoirs .
Supreme Court, *Swaraj Abhiyan v. Union of India* (2016): ordered the drought manual updated and the National Disaster Mitigation Fund set up .

Drought is handled by the Ministry of Agriculture (with pest attacks, hailstorm, frost/cold wave); MHA handles other notified disasters (LENSD 27 Aug 2026). The NADAMS satellite system monitors agricultural drought (APP).
Not in your sources: the rainfall threshold for "chronically drought-prone".

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 4 Geography › D-2 › India - rainfall distribution, variability, El Nino linkage, drought and flood-prone areas › Drought-prone areas - thresholds, share of land, chronic regions
bullets: About 68% of India's agricultural (cultivable) land is drought-prone in varying degrees (PYQ 2023 key).
Chronic drought: western India - Rajasthan, Gujarat (PYQ 2025), rain-shadow Deccan; in AP Rayalaseema and south Prakasam (NE monsoon failure + groundwater depletion) (CDI).
Types: meteorological (rain deficit), agricultural (soil moisture), hydrological (river/groundwater), flash drought (sudden heat + no rain) (LENS Jun 2025).

Manual for Drought Management (2016, revised 2020) uses rainfall deficit, vegetation, soil moisture and water indicators for declaration [GK]. Not in your sources: exact trigger thresholds of the current Manual.

bullets: Great Indian Bustard (Ardeotis nigriceps [GK]) is called Godawan and is Rajasthan's state bird. It is Critically Endangered (APP), with fewer than 150 birds left (CDI).
Conservation breeding is run in Jaisalmer, Rajasthan . The GIB is one of MoEFCC's five new national species projects and is on the Species Recovery Programme (APPCA 2026).
M.K. Ranjitsinh v. Union of India (2024) concerned the Great Indian Bustard (APPSC-GS 2024). GIB population under 150; the Supreme Court ordered underground power lines in its habitat (CDI).
GIB: CR, Rajasthan state bird (Godawan); in AP, Rollapadu WLS (Nandyal). GIB is in the species recovery programme and the national projects list (APPCA 2026).

bullets: Current relevance: Data-centre capacity reached 1.57 GW (2026) (LENSD 17 Sep 2026). The ES 2025-26 says rising data-centre capacity enables cloud, AI, IoT and 5G.

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 5 Science, Tech & Environment › 19 › Artificial intelligence and machine learning - concepts, applications, national AI strategy, ethical concerns › Ethical concerns - bias, deepfakes, privacy, facial recognition, jobs, explainability
bullets: Bias comes from training data that is not representative. Health AI trained on urban/Western data misses India's diversity (LENS Aug 2026). Facial-recognition accuracy varies with lighting, pose and demographics.
Deepfakes are made with GANs, diffusion models and large neural nets, and come as text, voice, image or video.
Privacy and surveillance: identification without consent, mass surveillance, predictive policing that threatens due process.
Job displacement in both manual and intellectual work. Explainability: deep models are "black boxes" whose decisions are hard to justify .

sections.topic: PESA Act 1996; Fifth and Sixth Schedule areas and tribal self-governance
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-3 › PESA Act 1996; Fifth and Sixth Schedule areas and tribal self-governance › PESA Act 1996 - committee, states, Gram Sabha powers
bullets: Needed because Art. 243M excludes Scheduled and tribal areas from Part IX. Art. 243M(4)(b) lets Parliament extend it, and such a law is not an amendment under Art. 368.

Gram Sabha (at para/majra/tola level) and Panchayats get powers over: intoxicants; ownership of minor forest produce; preventing tribal land alienation and restoring unlawfully alienated land; village markets; money-lending to STs; social-sector institutions; local plans and tribal sub-plans.

Higher-level panchayats must not usurp Gram Sabha powers. States should follow the Sixth Schedule pattern for district-level (Zila Panchayat) arrangements. Inconsistent state laws lapse one year after assent.

Zila Panchayat in Scheduled Areas: plans minor water bodies, controls social-sector institutions and Tribal Sub-Plans, and does other functions conferred by the State (CGPSC 2016 - "all of the above").
Operationalises Art. 243M(4)(b): extends Part IX (Panchayats) to Fifth Schedule Areas with exceptions (VIS 2026, CDX); recognises governance through customary law (VIS).

bullets: Red and yellow: Formation / parent material Crystalline igneous rocks (granite, gneiss) under low rainfall; Key traits Red from iron oxide, yellow when hydrated ; 5.18 lakh sq km; Main regions Kanyakumari-Jhansi, Kutch-Rajmahal (APP)
Arid/desert: Formation / parent material Wind-laid sand, low rainfall; Key traits Sandy, saline, low humus and N; kankar lower down; Main regions W Rajasthan

Black (regur / black cotton): Area / share 5.47 lakh sq km, 16.6%; Origin and properties From basalt (Deccan Trap); clay >62%; high moisture retention; deep cracks, "self-ploughing"; neutral to alkaline; rich in Ca, K, Mg, poor in N, P, humus; Where Maharashtra, Gujarat, MP, W. AP, N. Karnataka; Crops Cotton, jowar, chillies, tobacco

Red and yellow: Area / share 5.18 lakh sq km; Origin and properties Red from iron oxide; porous, light; poor in lime, humus, phosphoric acid; low moisture retention; Where Kanyakumari-Jhansi, Kutch-Rajmahal; Crops Ragi, groundnut, tobacco

Peaty soils form where heavy rainfall and high humidity keep soil waterlogged and organic matter piles up (APP). (The OCR answer key of the APPSC-G1 2024 peaty-soil question reads "semi-arid climate with salinity", which describes saline soils. Follow the waterlogged-organic description.)

bullets: Kharif: Food-grain area 2023-24 18.13 lakh ha; Food-grain area 2024-25 20.36 lakh ha; Paddy area 2024-25 14.04 lakh ha
The 2024-25 rise (+12.85% area) followed an 11.7% rainfall surplus, after a 16.5% deficit in 2023-24.

Kharif 2026 is a drought season: all 28 districts are in deficit (25 deficit, 3 large-deficit). By 19 Aug only 18.9 lakh ha was sown, about 61% of the normal 30.84 lakh ha. Groundnut was at 34% of normal, paddy 62%, maize 61%, pulses 70%, cotton 75% (CDCA Aug 2026).

bullets: The RBI (Amendment) Act, 2016 inserted Sections 45Z to 45ZO into the RBI Act, 1934 (APPCA). APPSC-GS 2022 key: amended in 2016.

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 5 Science, Tech & Environment › 22 › Species-specific conservation projects - Project Tiger, Project Elephant, Gangetic dolphin, Great Indian Bustard, vulture, cheetah reintroduction › Project Cheetah and International Big Cat Alliance
bullets: Project Cheetah brought 8 cheetahs from Namibia (17 Sep 2022) and 12 from South Africa (Feb 2023) to Kuno NP (Sheopur, MP). Counting cubs born in India, there are about 30 (APP). More cubs have since been born to a South African female (VIS Apr 2026).
The animals are African cheetahs, not the Asiatic cheetah, which survives only in Iran.
The cheetah was declared extinct in India in 1952 . The SC first ruled on reintroduction in 2012 (APP).
IBCA: launched in April 2023 to mark 50 years of Project Tiger. It is a treaty-based body covering 7 big cats: tiger, lion, leopard, snow leopard, cheetah, jaguar and puma.
Release site: Kuno NP, Sheopur (MP), on the Kuno river. Population with India-born cubs about 30 (APP).

Project Cheetah (17 Sep 2022) was the world's first intercontinental large-carnivore translocation. Gandhi Sagar WLS is the 2nd home and Veerangana Durgavati TR the 3rd. Population: 53 (APPCA 2026).

sections.topic: India and the WTO · Agreement on Agriculture
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-3 › India and the WTO - agreements, ministerial conferences, public stockholding, fisheries subsidies, appellate body crisis › Agreement on Agriculture - subsidy boxes, de minimis, market access
bullets: AoA (1995) has three pillars: domestic support, market access, export competition.
Green: What it covers Research, disease control, infrastructure, food security, direct income support not linked to production; Treatment Not trade-distorting; no limits
Blue: What it covers Direct payments that limit production (production-limiting programmes); Treatment Trade-distorting but exempt from cuts
Amber: What it covers All other support tied to prices/quantities - MSP, power, fertiliser, seed, irrigation subsidies (measured as AMS); Treatment Trade-distorting; subject to reduction
De minimis (Amber support allowed without penalty): 5% of value of agricultural output for developed, 10% for developing countries.

bullets: Rayalaseema lies in the rain-shadow of the Western and Eastern Ghats; low, erratic rainfall (APPCA Jan 2026).

Response: Pre-Monsoon Dry Sowing in Kurnool (target 92,000 acres; millets, pulses, oilseeds, Jeevamrutham) (APPCA Jul 2026); Veligonda Phase-I moves Krishna water to Prakasam, Nellore, Kadapa (APPCA Jan 2026).

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 4 Geography › D-2 › India - rainfall distribution, variability, El Nino linkage, drought and flood-prone areas › Drought-prone areas - thresholds, share of land, chronic regions
bullets: About 68% of India's agricultural (cultivable) land is drought-prone in varying degrees (PYQ 2023 key).
Chronic drought: western India - Rajasthan, Gujarat (PYQ 2025), rain-shadow Deccan; in AP Rayalaseema and south Prakasam (NE monsoon failure + groundwater depletion) (CDI).
Types: meteorological (rain deficit), agricultural (soil moisture), hydrological (river/groundwater), flash drought (sudden heat + no rain) (LENS Jun 2025).

Manual for Drought Management (2016, revised 2020) uses rainfall deficit, vegetation, soil moisture and water indicators for declaration [GK]. Not in your sources: exact trigger thresholds of the current Manual.

bullets: Drought and low density: population density is low because of recurring droughts and famines (APP). Rayalaseema has 8 districts (Kurnool, Nandyal, Anantapur, Sri Satya Sai, YSR, Annamayya, Tirupati, Chittoor).
Polavaram-Nallamala Sagar link: Status / aim Proposed, to carry Godavari surplus to Rayalaseema
Veligonda (Krishna to Gundlakamma): Status / aim 71.5% complete; Rs 768 crore paid to 6,206 displaced families; Phase II adds 3.283 lakh acres (CDCA Aug 2026)

Strengths: a Horticulture Hub, holding 43% of AP's horticulture area and 52% of its output, with 71% of micro-irrigation. Six AP districts are in India's top 10 for micro-irrigation: five from Rayalaseema plus Prakasam.
Industrial backwardness: investment is skewed towards the coast. Rayalaseema lacks anchor industries, which leads to distress migration and agrarian crisis (CDI Block10).

sections.topic: Devaluation vs depreciation, appreciation vs revaluation
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-3 › Exchange rate systems and rupee movement; currency internationalisation › Devaluation vs depreciation, appreciation vs revaluation - meaning and trade effects
bullets: Depreciation: Regime Flexible/floating; What happens Exchange rate rises - more rupees per dollar; Done by Market demand-supply

Devaluation is an expenditure-switching policy: home goods become cheaper for foreigners and imports costlier at home, so spending switches to home-produced goods; it is a recognised method (with exchange depreciation, exchange control, monetary/fiscal measures, import curbs) to correct BoP disequilibrium.
Devaluation/depreciation makes exports cheaper (in foreign currency) and imports dearer, so the trade balance tends to improve - it does not raise export prices.
ES 2025-26: a weaker currency helps India's trade balance more than it hurts the financial channel (capital outflows); net impact positive.

Rupee: 5.4% depreciation in FY26 (to Jan), among the most depreciated with the yen (ES 2025-26); crossed 96.2/$ on 18-19 May 2026, down 6.3% since 1 Jan 2026, on Brent at $110.8 and FPI outflows (TH, 19 May 2026).

Deepfakes are made with GANs, diffusion models and large neural nets, and come as text, voice, image or video.

Job displacement in both manual and intellectual work. Explainability: deep models are "black boxes" whose decisions are hard to justify .

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 5 Science, Tech & Environment › 19 › Emerging technology frontiers - artificial intelligence, quantum computing, robotics, 3D printing, advanced materials › Quantum computing - qubit, superposition, entanglement, supremacy
bullets: Qubit can be 0, 1 or any state between (superposition); entanglement links qubits regardless of distance; decoherence (loss of quantum state through the environment) is the main barrier (TH, 9 Jul 2026).
Entanglement sudden death = abrupt total loss of entanglement; Raman Research Institute showed one well-timed local "quantum flip" can delay or prevent it (LENS daily, 16 Sep 2026).
DST quantum-safe report: post-quantum cryptography migration for Critical Information Infrastructure by 2029, others by 2033 (LENS daily, 31 May 2026).

Supremacy machines: Google Sycamore (2019) ; China's photonic Jiuzhang (2020) . Micius (China, 2016) = first quantum communication satellite . Microsoft's Majorana 2 chip raised qubit stability to 20-60 s (APPCA, 2026).
2025 = International Year of Quantum Science and Technology (UN; centenary of quantum mechanics) ; World Quantum Day = 14 April.

bullets: Insolvency is a financial state: being unable to pay debts as they fall due. Bankruptcy is the legal declaration that follows (BPSC 2023 key: the two statements reversing these are wrong) .
IBBI (2016): Role Regulator of insolvency professionals, IP agencies, information utilities, registered valuers; frames CIRP/liquidation regulations

IBC Amendment Act 2026: NCLT must admit or reject a CIRP plea within 14 days. It adds a Creditor-Initiated Insolvency Resolution Process (CIIRP), a hybrid of debtor-in-possession and creditor-in-control, plus an out-of-court route (LENS Jun 2026; TH 31 Mar and 15 Jun 2026).

Insolvency = the *state* of being unable to pay debts when due; bankruptcy = the *legal* declaration/process for an insolvent individual or firm . BPSC 2023 swapped the two definitions, making those statements false.

Enacted 28 May 2016 on the T.K. Viswanathan Committee (Bankruptcy Law Reforms Committee, 2015); replaced SICA and scattered Companies Act provisions with one time-bound, creditor-in-control process (APPCA Jun 2026).

bullets: LNG: Key facts natural gas cooled below -160 C, which shrinks its volume 1,000 times; lighter than air (VIS; TH 2 Apr 2026)
CNG: Key facts natural gas compressed to 200-250 kg/cm2; vehicle fuel (VIS)
LPG: Key facts propane + butane; a by-product of oil refining and gas processing; heavier than air (TH; LENS)
Natural gas is the cleanest fossil fuel . Brent (North Sea) and WTI (US) are the crude price benchmarks . Furnace oil is a heavy residual fuel for boilers .
India has 33 crore LPG connections. Domestic gas could supply 30 crore if they switched to PNG (PNGRB, TH Apr 2026).

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 5 Science, Tech & Environment › 21 › Other renewables - biomass, biofuels (National Policy on Biofuels, ethanol blending), small hydro, geothermal, tidal, waste-to-energy › Biogas and biomass - constituents, microbes, gobar gas, bagasse cogeneration, CBG (SATAT, GOBARdhan)
bullets: Microbes: methanogenic archaea (methanogens) carry out the final methane-forming step (CDI); gobar gas = biogas from cattle dung.
Compressed Biogas (CBG) = purified, compressed biogas, chemically identical to CNG; renewable, carbon-neutral (TH, 14 Jul 2026).
GOBARdhan (Galvanizing Organic Bio-Agro Resources Dhan), 2018: Key fact Umbrella for converting cattle dung, farm solid waste to compost, biogas, CBG/bio-CNG
Biomass energy = solar energy stored by plants in photosynthesis; burned directly or converted to biogas/biofuels. Gobar gas is biomass energy (APPSC 2019).

Biogas = mainly methane + CO2 with traces of other gases, formed by anaerobic digestion of organic matter; methane is ~50-75% ; produced by methanogenic bacteria (methanogens) in the absence of oxygen . Slurry left behind is a good organic manure.

Compressed Biogas Obligation (CBO) in CGD: 1% / 3% / 4% of CNG/PNG consumption in FY 2025-26 / 2026-27 / 2027-28, then 5% from 2028-29. The aim is to substitute LNG imports (IYB 2026).

Methanol = low-carbon hydrogen-carrier fuel from high-ash coal, agri-residue, CO2 from thermal plants, natural gas; replaces petrol/diesel in transport, DG sets, boilers; partly LPG, kerosene in cooking (IYB).

sections.topic: Right to Constitutional Remedies · Mandamus limits
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-1 › Right to Constitutional Remedies - Article 32; the five writs and their scope › Mandamus limits - making law, policy, private bodies
bullets: Mandamus is not issued to the Government to make a law; it cannot lie in the absence of a policy, but once a policy is laid down its terms can be enforced (PYQ A-R G2 2025: both true, R explains A).
Not against private individuals/bodies; not for discretionary functions or legislative functions.
Mandamus also not against a private individual/body, the President or Governors, to enforce a discretionary duty or a non-statutory departmental instruction .
Only habeas corpus runs against private persons; SC writs only for FRs, not statutory rights (APP; UPSC).
Res judicata: if an HC dismisses a writ on merits, the same plea cannot go to the SC under Art. 32 - only in appeal; if dismissed not on merits, SC can be moved (UPSC).

bullets: Vacating office (Art. 179): he ceases to be a member, resigns to the Deputy Speaker, or is removed by a resolution of a majority of all the then members, with 14 days' notice.

sections.where: Rocket Sheets · Indian Polity › #71 · Supreme Court and High Court Judges
bullets: Supreme Court Judges are governed under Part V, Chapter IV of the Constitution.
The Governor has no power to appoint High Court Judges.
A distinguished jurist is eligible for appointment as a Supreme Court Judge under Article 124(3)(c).
The President transfers High Court Judges on the advice of a collegium led by the Chief Justice of India.

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-2 › High Courts and subordinate judiciary; judicial review, judicial activism, PIL and judicial overreach debate › High Court judges - appointment, transfer, resignation, removal instances, writ and supervisory powers, contempt
bullets: Under Art. 217, the President appoints after consulting the CJI and the Governor, and for puisne judges also the HC Chief Justice. Proposals start with the HC Chief Justice and the HC collegium (CJ + 2), then go to the SC collegium (CJI + 2 senior-most judges) (LENSD 12 Aug 2026).
The inquiry report on Yashwant Varma (formerly Allahabad HC) was to be tabled despite his resignation (LENSD 11 Jul 2026).

Contempt: Arts. 129 and 215 make the SC and HCs courts of record. The Contempt of Courts Act, 1971 followed the H.N. Sanyal Committee and defines civil contempt (wilful disobedience) and criminal contempt (scandalising or obstructing justice). Fair criticism and accurate reporting are exceptions (VIS 2026).
Art. 215: every HC is a court of record; punishes contempt of itself and subordinate courts (SC: Art. 129).

Appellate: primarily a court of appeal; second civil appeals on questions of law only; death sentences of Sessions Courts need HC confirmation (now under BNSS 2023, which replaced CrPC from 1 July 2024) .

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-2 › Governor - appointment, powers, discretionary powers, position and controversies (Article 200/201, Article 356 reports) › Appointment and office - Articles 153-158, same Governor for two states, qualifications, pleasure (B.P. Singhal)
bullets: Art. 155: appointed by the President by warrant under hand and seal. The Governor is neither directly nor indirectly elected.

The term is 5 years, but he continues until his successor enters office . So "quits office immediately after the term expires" is the wrong statement (APPSC-G1 2019). He resigns to the President, may be transferred, and may be reappointed.

In B.P. Singhal v. UoI (2010), the pleasure doctrine is not unfettered: a Governor cannot be removed arbitrarily or merely because the Centre's government changes, and removal is open to limited judicial review . No grounds for removal are stated in the Constitution.
Grounds for removal are not stated in the Constitution. The President may transfer a Governor, and a Governor may be reappointed (APP).

Art 200 reservation: mandatory for bills endangering the High Court's position (APP; IYB). The President has an absolute veto over reserved bills (APP). APPSC 2025 key: reservation is an example of central control over states.

sections.topic: Forest and wildlife legal framework · National Forest Policy 1952 and 1988
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 5 Science, Tech & Environment › 22 › Forest and wildlife legal framework - Indian Forest Act 1927, Forest (Conservation) Act 1980, Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972 › National Forest Policy 1952 and 1988 - objectives and forest-cover target
bullets: 1952: one-third of the land under forest, with 60% in hills and 25% in plains .
1988: 33% of the geographical area under forest or tree cover, and two-thirds (66%) in hilly and mountainous regions (CDCA Jul 2026).

NFP 1988 objectives: ecological stability; conserving natural heritage; checking soil erosion and desert spread; massive afforestation and social forestry; meeting the fuelwood, fodder and minor forest produce needs of tribal and rural people; and a massive people's movement involving women. It also backs corridors between protected areas and fuel-efficient chulhas .
Exam angle: the statement "at least two-thirds of the country's land should be under forest" is NOT true (APPSC 2024). Two-thirds applies only to the hills.

sections.topic: Impacts of climate change on India · Heat stress and health
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 5 Science, Tech & Environment › 22 › Impacts of climate change on India - monsoon, agriculture, Himalayan glaciers, sea-level rise, extreme events › Heat stress and health - wet-bulb limit, Heat Action Plans, vector-borne diseases
bullets: A wet-bulb temperature of about 35°C is the limit of human survivability, because above it sweat can no longer cool the body . The World Bank warned that India could be among the first places to cross it routinely (UPSC 2025).
A CMIP6 study finds around 40 coastal districts could warm by more than 1°C by 2040. Kerala and Tamil Nadu could see wet-bulb temperatures of about 31°C (LENSD 7 Jun 2026).
Heat Action Plans: Ahmedabad drew up the first one in South Asia, in 2013 .

The Dasra report "Under the Weather" finds that nearly 40% of districts face high risk from extreme weather. Warmer, wetter conditions are expanding dengue and malaria, floods bring cholera and hepatitis, and heat brings heatstroke and cardiovascular strain (TH 10 Apr 2026). Urban waterlogging, as in Mumbai, spreads leptospirosis, typhoid and hepatitis A (TH 7 Apr 2026).

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-4 › Indian tax system - direct and indirect taxes, tax buoyancy, tax-GDP ratio, progressivity › Direct vs indirect taxes - classification and base
bullets: Direct tax: impact and incidence fall on the same person, cannot be shifted; administered by CBDT (Central Boards of Revenue Act, 1963). Indirect tax: collected by an intermediary (seller) and passed on to the consumer through price; administered by CBIC.
Income tax: Type Direct; Base on which levied Income of individuals, HUFs, firms, trusts
Corporation tax: Type Direct; Base on which levied Net profit of companies (22% base rate, effective ~25.17%)
Customs duty: Type Indirect; Base on which levied Imports/exports (Customs Act, 1962)
Estate duty, gift tax (abolished): Indirect (burden shifted to consumer) Entertainment, luxury, entry taxes

bullets: Delete "during the pleasure of the President" from Article 156. The Governor should be removed only by impeachment by the State Legislature, on the same lines as the President's impeachment.
Governors should not be made Chancellors of universities or given other statutory roles, so that the office stays out of day-to-day clashes with State governments.

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-4 › Monetary policy - objectives, instruments (CRR, SLR, repo, reverse repo, MSF, OMO, LAF), transmission › Liquidity conditions and transmission - surplus vs deficit
bullets: Surplus liquidity speeds up transmission and pulls market rates below the repo. Deficit liquidity weakens it.
In Dec 2025, currency leakage, tax outflows and reserve needs tightened liquidity, so RBI injected ₹1 lakh crore through OMO plus a $5 bn swap (LENS, Dec 2025).

RBI has said it will keep "sufficient liquidity" to help transmission (Governor, Feb 2026, TH). By 3 Sep 2026 the surplus had reached about ₹10.32 lakh crore, and RBI began draining it through VRRR (TH, 5 Sep 2026).

bullets: Signed by the Government of India and RBI in 2015; formally adopted flexible inflation targeting (CDI).
Government sets the target. RBI must keep CPI inflation at 4% +/- 2% and is answerable to the Government when it misses (APP; CDI).

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-4 › Inflation - types, causes, measurement (CPI, WPI, core inflation), effects and control measures › Control measures - monetary, fiscal, supply-side
bullets: Monetary (RBI): Tools Raise repo rate, CRR, OMO sales, anchor expectations; repo held at 5.25% (Aug 2026) with an October hike expected (TH, 8 Aug, 16 Sep 2026)

Supply-side: Tools OMSS (Domestic) - FCI sells wheat and rice at fixed prices; Price Stabilisation Fund buffer of pulses and onions; subsidised Bharat Atta, Bharat Rice, Bharat Dal (Bharat Chana Dal from July 2023 at ₹60/kg)
Monetary: Examples Raise repo rate, CRR; sell securities through OMOs; tighten liquidity
Supply-side: Examples Buffer stock release: 47,786 MT of onion from the PSF buffer by NCCF and NAFED (to 8 Oct 2025, IYB); OMSS sale of wheat and rice
Limitation: the repo rate is a demand-side tool and cannot fix supply shocks such as onion prices or crude oil (CDI).

sections.topic: Agrarian crisis · National Commission on Farmers (Swaminathan)
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-3 › Agrarian crisis - causes, farmer distress and suicides, loan waivers, small-holding viability › National Commission on Farmers (Swaminathan) - year, reports, MSP formula
bullets: Constituted 18 November 2004 (answer to "which year": 2004), chaired by Prof. M.S. Swaminathan; set up to address the calamity of farmer suicides; submitted five reports (2004-06) .
MSP formula: C2 + 50% (C2 = A2 + family labour + imputed rent/interest on owned land and capital).
Other recommendations: land reforms, secure rights for women and tenants, universal crop insurance, National Agricultural Risk Fund, affordable credit.
Core vision: farming should become economically viable and ecologically sustainable, and farmers' quality of life should improve (CDI).
Other recommendations: land reforms, irrigation, cheaper institutional credit, crop insurance and market reforms. The National Policy for Farmers, 2007 drew on its reports .

bullets: Women operated 12.8% of holdings in 2010-11, rising to 13.9% in 2015-16 (UPSC; the PYQ key is 12.8%). LENS (Jun 2025) quotes 12.8% of holdings and 10.34% of area without naming the census round.
Size classes above are the standard Agriculture Census classes ; "small and marginal farmers" = holdings up to 2 ha.
Small and marginal farmers are about 86.2% of all farmers but hold only about 47% of the crop area (APPCA, May 2026).
Census 2010-11 (PYQ-tested): small + marginal holdings were about 85% of holdings but operated only about 44% of the area; women-operated holdings were 12.8% of all operational holdings.
An operational holding is all land used for agricultural production and operated as one technical unit by one person, alone or with others, regardless of title, size or location.

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-4 › Globalisation and society - culture, migration, labour, inequality; the anti-globalisation critique › Impact on women, tribals, farmers and traditional artisans
bullets: Farmers: fear of cheap imports under WTO rules; the rise in farmer suicides linked to debt and crop failure was especially marked in Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh (UPSC).
Small growers: 98% of coffee growers are small farmers facing global price swings and competition from Brazil and Vietnam (CDI).
Women: self-employed women nearly tripled since 2017-18 (IYB). 48% of rural women are migrants, against 5.9% of men (LENS Nov 2025).
Artisans and domestic firms: squeezed by MNC competition, which can mean shutdowns and layoffs. Skilled labour moves to MNCs while unskilled labour stays behind (APP).

bullets: Voluntary for all farmers since 2020; covers pre-sowing to post-harvest, localised risks; from Kharif 2026 also wild-animal attack and paddy inundation losses (VIS, Apr 2026).

RWBCIS = weather-index based payouts. AP gave free crop insurance 2019-24 ; reintroduced voluntary enrolment from Rabi 2024-25 (farmer pays small share of actuarial rate, rest split equally Centre-State): 34.93 lakh farmers in 2024 (APSES) → 10.63 lakh farmers, 11.81 lakh ha (CDI SES 2025-26).

PMFBY (2016) replaced NAIS and MNAIS. It is a Central Sector Scheme: the Centre's premium subsidy goes straight to insurers. It covers pre-sowing to post-harvest losses, including localised calamities (IYB; CDI).

Scale: 4.19 crore farmers insured in 2024-25, 32% more than 2022-23 (ES 2025-26). Over nine years: 78.62 crore applications and ₹1,82,136 crore in claims (IYB 2026). Tech: YES-TECH (remote-sensing yield estimation), WINDS (weather stations), DigiClaim.

Kharif 2026: CM ordered that every cultivated crop be insured, with Collectors accountable; enrolment closed 31 July, paddy 15 August (TH, 29 Jul 2026). The AP Rythu Sangham wants free insurance restored (TH, 15 Jul 2026).

bullets: Consumption: NSS / HCES (MoSPI). Official estimates rest on this, and inequality looks lower than on other measures (TH 7 May 2026).

Income: no official income survey. Estimates use PLFS wages, tax data and the World Inequality Database. WID shows income inequality rising: median earnings of the top 10% were 13 times those of the bottom 10% in 2023-24 (IYB 2026).

Leaders: Kanneganti Hanumanthu (killed in police firing at Minchalapadu, 26 Feb 1922; CDX misprints 2022); Congress men Unnava Lakshmi Narayana and Madabhushi Vedantam Narasimhachari studied and backed it; Konda Venkatappayya tried to dilute it (Congress had asked only for social boycott, not tax refusal).
Repression: 28 men and 8 women arrested; Unnava jailed (wrote the play *Nayakuralu* in jail); normalcy by March 1922.

bullets: El Nino = abnormal warming of the central and eastern equatorial Pacific; an unusual warm current flows southwards along the Peru (west South American) coast, replacing the cold Peruvian (Humboldt) current. It flows in the Pacific Ocean.
Rising air shifts east, air descends over the Indian Ocean - high pressure there, delayed/weak Indian monsoon, drought; lower summer-crop (rice, sugarcane) yields, food inflation, harsher heat.
Historically 6 of 10 El Nino years brought depressed Indian rainfall; the last global El Nino was 2023-24 (TH, 1 Feb 2026).
Exam angle: El Nino is a climate pattern, not a storm; statement sets on Peru warm current, 3-7-year recurrence and meaning of the name.

About 10% of annual rainfall is pre-monsoon; useful for rice, jute, coffee, mango, tea (APP).
Dust aerosols heat the mid-troposphere over the Indo-Gangetic plain, helping pull the monsoon inland (LENSD, 3 Jun 2026).
Nautapa is the traditional nine-day peak of summer heat in north India, just before the monsoon arrives (LENS Jun 2026).

bullets: Art. 329(a): laws on delimitation and allotment of seats cannot be questioned in court; Art. 329(b): an election can be challenged only by an election petition .

By convention courts do not interfere once the poll process begins; the ECI cannot review a result. Petitions go to the High Court (Parliament, state legislatures) and the Supreme Court for President/VP (Art. 71) (UPSC).

Art. 329(b): an election to Parliament or a state legislature can be questioned only by an election petition under the RPA 1951. Such petitions are tried by the High Court, with appeal to the Supreme Court .
President/VP election disputes: decided by the Supreme Court (Art. 71) .
The ECI does not try election petitions. It decides party and symbol disputes and advises on disqualification.

For misbehaviour the President must refer the matter to the Supreme Court (Art. 317); removal only if the SC upholds the cause - its advice is binding. The President (Governor for SPSC) may suspend the member during the inquiry.
UPSC: Appointed by President; Removed by President; Age limit 65; Resigns to President
President appoints an Acting Chairman during vacancy/absence of the Chairman.

Removal grounds: insolvency, paid employment outside duties, infirmity of mind or body; and misbehaviour only after reference to the Supreme Court, whose advice is binding (Art. 317). President may suspend the member during the SC inquiry.

Then Bihar (March 1947) to calm riots against Muslims .
15 August 1947: Gandhi was in Calcutta (Beliaghata), fasting and praying, not at the Delhi celebrations ; Mountbatten called him a "one-man boundary force" .

bullets: Inviter: Rajkumar Shukla, a local indigo cultivator (agriculturist) of Champaran, persuaded Gandhi to come and investigate the peasants' condition (met Gandhi at the Lucknow Congress, 1916 ). Rajendra Prasad was an associate, not the inviter.

Action: Gandhi defied the official order to leave the district (Motihari ); he and his lawyers toured villages recording peasants' complaints against forced indigo cultivation; this forced a government inquiry.
Outcome: Committee with Gandhi as a member; Champaran Agrarian Act (1918) abolished the Tinkathia system; refund of 25% of illegal exactions.
Rajendra Prasad, Brajkishore Prasad, Anugrah Narayan Sinha: Profession / role Lawyers of Bihar (vakils)
Exam angle: statement pairs on "who invited" and "which state" (Champaran is in Bihar, not Gujarat).

bullets: National Monsoon Mission launched 2012 by the Ministry of Earth Sciences (IITM Pune + IMD) .

bullets: NPIT 2012: uses ICT as a driver of growth, jobs, governance reform and inclusion.
Twin goals: bring the full power of ICT within reach of the whole of India, and make India the Global Hub and Destination for IT and ITES Services by 2020.

Context: Indian IT was a USD 100 billion industry in 2011-12, 80% of revenue from exports; six hubs (Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Pune, NCR) had ~90% of the industry and were near saturation, so the policy pushed IT into Tier II and Tier III cities.
Objectives: strengthen the global IT position; generate jobs; use ICT in education, health, skills, financial inclusion and governance; e-literacy for all.
The later Digital India, Aadhaar, UPI, BharatNet and DigiLocker are described as putting NPIT's vision into practice (CDI).

bullets: It merges 9 laws (EPF, ESI, Maternity Benefit, Gratuity, Unorganised Workers' Social Security Act, etc.). The four Labour Codes came into force on 21 Nov 2025, with the 2026 Central Rules (CDI Block15).

It recognises gig workers, platform workers and aggregators in law for the first time. Aggregators pay 1-2% of annual turnover (capped at 5% of payouts) into a social security fund. A National Social Security Board recommends schemes (CDI; LENS Jul 2025). Maternity leave stays at 26 weeks; a creche is required at 50+ employees.

e-Shram (26 Aug 2021, MoLE): Aadhaar-verified National Database of Unorganised Workers; 12-digit UAN; age 16-59; excludes income-tax payers and EPFO/ESIC members. The 2024 One-Stop Solution joins up 15 schemes; 31.87 crore registered (LENSD, 26 Aug and 16 Aug 2026).

bullets: Normal (canonical) El Nino: maximum warming in the eastern Pacific near Peru .
El Nino Modoki ("similar but different", Japanese): maximum warming in the central Pacific, with cooler waters on both the eastern and western sides (tripole) .

bullets: El Nino: central/east equatorial Pacific at least 0.5°C warmer for five consecutive overlapping 3-month periods; 6 of 10 El Nino years give weak Indian monsoons (TH, 1 Feb 2026).
La Nina generally strengthens the monsoon, brings colder winters and more Bay cyclones (VIS 2026).
Deficient years cited: 2015 (actual 86% of LPA - one of the worst droughts), 2023 (El Nino 2023-24) (TH, 14 Apr 2026).
IOD: positive IOD can offset El Nino (TH, 1 Jul 2026).

bullets: Wheat and paddy: FCI and State agencies buy all stock that meets specifications at MSP, so procurement is effectively open-ended. Coarse grains: States procure with GoI's prior approval (IYB 2026). Pulses, oilseeds and copra: limited PSS procurement (25% cap).
Wheat RMS 2026-27: >35 MT procured (+17%), above the 34.5 MT target (30 MT the year before). Punjab 12.1 MT and MP 10.4 MT led. Output was 120.65 MT (TH, 4 Jun 2026).
Decentralised Procurement (DCP), 1997: States procure, store and distribute; the Centre reimburses economic cost minus CIP (UPSC notes).

AP: State agencies procure paddy for FCI's Central Pool under the Paddy Procurement Scheme. DBT to farmers is due within a 48-hour window (APPCA Mar 2026; APSES 2024-25). DCMS societies procure so that farmers actually get MSP. APMARKFED is the apex cooperative marketing body (APSES 2024-25).

bullets: NTR Bharosa Pension (earlier YSR Pension Kanuka): ₹4,000/month to old-age and widow pensioners, enhanced from ₹3,000 w.e.f. April 2024 (APSES 2024-25).
Jan 2026: monthly distribution automated with Aadhaar-based biometric authentication to remove ghost beneficiaries; AP tops up the central NSAP pension from its own funds (APPCA).
2019-24: Name YSR Pension Kanuka (CDI quiz); Monthly amount (old age / widow) Raised in steps to ₹3,000 (APSES)

Scale: 61.92 lakh beneficiaries; ₹2,693 crore released for 1 Sep 2026; ₹73,506 crore spent on pensions since June 2024 (TH, 31 Aug 2026; earlier 63.12 lakh in Dec 2025, the largest share BC at 28.32 lakh). sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-6 › Important flagship programmes of the Central Government - social sector (health, education, nutrition, housing) › Code on Social Security 2020 - gig and platform workers, e-Shram, unorganised workers
bullets: It merges 9 laws (EPF, ESI, Maternity Benefit, Gratuity, Unorganised Workers' Social Security Act, etc.). The four Labour Codes came into force on 21 Nov 2025, with the 2026 Central Rules (CDI Block15).

It recognises gig workers, platform workers and aggregators in law for the first time. Aggregators pay 1-2% of annual turnover (capped at 5% of payouts) into a social security fund. A National Social Security Board recommends schemes (CDI; LENS Jul 2025). Maternity leave stays at 26 weeks; a creche is required at 50+ employees.

e-Shram (26 Aug 2021, MoLE): Aadhaar-verified National Database of Unorganised Workers; 12-digit UAN; age 16-59; excludes income-tax payers and EPFO/ESIC members. The 2024 One-Stop Solution joins up 15 schemes; 31.87 crore registered (LENSD, 26 Aug and 16 Aug 2026).

Also: solitary confinement before rejection is illegal; 14 days between rejection and execution .
Epuru Sudhakar v Govt of AP (2006): pardon/remission is open to limited judicial review .

sections.where: Rocket Sheets · Indian Polity › #76 · Women’s Political Representation and Reservation
bullets: Women's political reservation was first constitutionally institutionalized through the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts, 1992.
Women's reservation in the House of the People covers seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
Women's reservation in the Legislative Assembly of the National Capital Territory of Delhi covers Scheduled Caste-reserved seats.
Not less than one-third of the total seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes under Article 243D(2) must be reserved for women belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
The mandatory sub-quota for Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe women within Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe reserved seats is one-third.

sections.where: Rocket Sheets · Indian Society › #9 · Constitutional Articles on Social Rights
bullets: Article 14 concerns women.
Article 14 concerns caste.
Article 15(1) prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
Article 15(4) provides special provisions for Scheduled Castes.
Article 46 provides for the promotion of Scheduled Caste interests.

sections.topic: Purity-pollution and cultural traits of caste

bullets: Dumont: hierarchy rests on the pure vs impure; *Homo Hierarchicus* vs *Homo Aequalis* (CDX).

Dipankar Gupta counters Dumont: castes are discrete communities and "difference" is not "hierarchy" (CDX).

bullets: The Seventh Schedule of the Act is the "List of Funds" in the Public Account, including provident, pension and insurance funds (APPSC 2022). Securities held against these funds are divided by population ratio (Sec 52).

Electricity (Twelfth Schedule): power from Central Generating Stations is shared on the actual consumption of the DISCOMs over the last 5 years. APGENCO plants go by location, and existing PPAs continue.
AP says this gave it about 46% of the power for 58% of the population (CDI Block13).

The APPSC-GS 2019 key marked "Gadgil formula" for the "electricity distribution formula" question. The Act's rule is the 5-year consumption basis. If the options force a choice, the key's answer is Gadgil.
A deficit State has first right of refusal on the other State's surplus power for 10 years.

sections.topic: Consuming vs producing states under destination-based tax
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-4 › Impact of GST on commerce, industry and state finances; unresolved GST issues › Consuming vs producing states under destination-based tax
bullets: GST is a destination-based consumption tax: revenue goes to the State where goods/services are consumed, not produced.
IGST on inter-state supply (Art. 269A) is levied by the Centre and apportioned; the destination state gets the state share.
Effect: consuming states gain, manufacturing states (e.g., Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka) feared loss - a key reason for the 5-year compensation guarantee .

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-5 › Basic features of the Andhra Pradesh economy after bifurcation - GSDP, growth rate, sectoral shares › Vision documents - goals and target years
bullets: Sunrise Andhra Pradesh Vision 2029: Launched 2016; Key targets Among top 3 States by 2022, best State by 2029, leading global destination by 2050

Swarna Andhra: "Wealthy, Healthy, Happy" State; 10 Padi Sutralu (Zero Poverty ... Deep Tech); foundation year 2025-26; medium-term GSDP ₹29.29 lakh cr by 2028-29 (16.45% a year); investment ₹40.43 lakh cr (77% private) (SES 2025-26).

Sunrise AP Vision 2029 (residual AP, after 2014): three staged goals: among the top three States by 2022 , the best State in India by 2029, and the most preferred global investment destination by 2050.
Exam angle: match the vision to its target year (2029 best State; 2050 investment destination; 2047 ₹308 lakh crore).

Padi Sutralu = 10 guiding principles (PYQ answer: 10): 1 Zero Poverty; 2 Population Management & HRD; 3 Skilling & Employment; 4 Water Security; 5 Farmer-Agri Tech; 6 Global Best Logistics; 7 Cost Optimisation in Energy & Fuel; 8 Product Perfection; 9 Swachh Andhra.

bullets: Background: allies refused to supply equipment and raw materials during the Indo-Pak war. The plan followed the Gadgil strategy of growth with stability and progress towards self-reliance.
agriculture growth 5% a year, industry 8-10%
exports to grow about 7% a year
an end to concessional PL-480 food imports by 1971

IMD "Observed Rainfall Variability and Changes over Andhra Pradesh": climate hot and humid, summer March-June; rainfall variability quite high (APPSC 2025 key).
Retreating monsoon: withdraws October-November; Bay of Bengal cyclones bring the rain of this season to the southern states.
SW monsoon (June-September) gives ~2/3 (65-70%) of AP's rainfall. It sets in during the 2nd week of June; July is the wettest month (CDI; APP).
Normal rainfall (APSES 2024-25): SWM 574.7 mm + NEM 285.3 mm = ~860 mm a year. CDI prints a State average of ~966 mm (older figure). 2024: SWM 681.6 mm (+18.6%); NEM 278.7 mm (-2.3%).
